l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: NSL Article 42(2) sets a no-bail-unless threshold for national security bail applications.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFA statement of the statutory text used in construing NSL Article 42(2).

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: For NSL bail, Article 42(2) introduces a threshold materially more stringent than ordinary bail under the Criminal Procedure Ordinance.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFA distinguishes the NSL Article 42 threshold from ordinary bail.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: NSL Article 42(2) operates as a specific exception within the existing bail regime, rather than replacing the whole bail regime.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFA frames NSL Article 42(2) as a special threshold within the wider bail system.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: When assessing NSL Article 42(2), the court may consider whether bail conditions affect the future risk assessment.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFA rejects a sealed-off first stage that excludes proposed bail conditions.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Appropriate bail conditions may be relevant to the risk assessment because they can deter breach or further offending.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFA connects conditions to risk management and deterrence.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFA summarised NSL Article 42(2) as a specific exception importing a stringent threshold for bail.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFA held that Tong (No 1) erred in a crucial respect by misapprehending the nature and effect of the NSL Article 42(2) threshold.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Lineage marker showing Lai limiting/correcting Tong on NSL bail threshold.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Tong treated Article 42(2) as targeting the risk of offending while on bail in respect of national security offences.
